name: Yu Suzuki
milestone_by_age_26: Designed and released Champion Boxing for Sega's SG-1000 in 1984 at age 26, his first major commercial game credit before Hang-On (1985) and later Virtua Fighter/Shenmue fame.
early_history_summary: Born June 10, 1958 in Kamaishi, Japan. Joined Sega after university, shipping Champion Boxing (1984) then reinventing arcade with Hang-On, Out Run, After Burner, Virtua Fighter, and Shenmue. Became Sega's defining arcade auteur.
family_context_summary: Born Kamaishi, Japan; detailed parental professions not strongly documented in reviewed English sources.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Sega arcade labs, Japan game industry 1980s, hardware experimentation
evidence_summary: Suzuki's Champion Boxing (1984, age 26) is a dated commercial milestone inside Sega before his more famous mid/late-20s arcade hits. Sega's hardware labs and Japan arcade frontier provided tools and ecosystem; family capital not documented.
starting_point: Born Kamaishi, Japan 1958; joined Sega after university into the arcade R&D culture.
current_position: Veteran game designer; YS Net founder after Sega; known for Shenmue series and arcade innovations; industry legend status.

trajectory.event: Released Champion Boxing for Sega SG-1000, first major design credit.
Created Hang-On, pioneering ride-on arcade cabinets.
Launched Virtua Fighter, defining 3D fighting games.
Released Shenmue on Dreamcast, ambitious open-world adventure.

name: Will Wright
milestone_by_age_26: Designed and published Raid on Bungeling Bay (1984) at age 24, then developed the systems that became SimCity (released 1989) after founding Maxis with Jeff Braun in 1987 (age 27—SimCity launch is post-26 but Bungeling Bay is the ≤26 commercial milestone).
early_history_summary: Born January 20, 1960 in Atlanta. Self-directed learner interested in models and systems; shipped Raid on Bungeling Bay commercially, then built city-simulation tools that became SimCity after cofounding Maxis.
family_context_summary: Born Atlanta; mother reportedly encouraged intellectual interests after father's early death (commonly cited in bios).
parent_family_domain_summary: Not a game-industry family; intellectual home environment more than commercial game dynasty.
primary_early_advantage_tags: systems thinking, early commercial game, Maxis later, simulation genre invention
evidence_summary: Wright shipped a commercial game at 24 (Raid on Bungeling Bay) and was already deep into SimCity design logic by mid-20s. Maxis/SimCity fame peaks after 26, but the ≤26 commercial design milestone is solid. Primary engine is scarce systems-design insight.
starting_point: Born Atlanta 1960; self-directed education and early computer game experimentation.
current_position: Legendary game designer; after Maxis/EA and Spore, pursued robotics/space interests (e.g., Stupid Fun Club era) and remains a defining simulation-game figure.

trajectory.event: Published Raid on Bungeling Bay, first commercial design credit.
Co-founded Maxis with Jeff Braun.
Released SimCity, creating the city-building simulation genre's mainstream hit.
The Sims launched, becoming one of the best-selling PC franchises.
Released Spore after ambitious multi-year development.

name: American McGee
category: Game designer (id Software, American McGee's Alice)
milestone_by_age_26: Joined id Software in the early 1990s (~age 21) and contributed to Doom/Quake-era titles as level designer/programmer before age 26; major commercial franchise work at the industry's technical frontier.
early_history_summary: Born December 13, 1972. Entered id Software as a young designer during Doom/Quake years, then moved to EA and created American McGee's Alice (2000). Later founded independent studios and continued Alice sequels.
family_context_summary: Difficult childhood commonly reported in profiles (instability/adversity narratives); exact financial details vary by source quality.
primary_early_advantage_tags: id Software, Doom/Quake era, Romero/Carmack orbit
evidence_summary: McGee's material ≤26 milestone is contribution to id Software's Doom/Quake generation while still young. Elite peer ecosystem at id is the dominant advantage; later Alice branded him as an auteur. Family platform was not an advantage.
starting_point: Born 1972; entered professional game development young via id Software during the 1990s FPS revolution.
current_position: Independent game designer/director associated with Alice franchise and studio ventures; industry cult-auteur profile.

trajectory.event: Joined id Software during the Doom era as a young designer.
Contributed to Quake-era development at id.
Released American McGee's Alice at Electronic Arts.
Released Alice: Madness Returns sequel.

name: Clifford 'CliffyB' Bleszinski
category: Game designer (Epic Games, Gears of War)
milestone_by_age_26: Designed Jazz Jackrabbit (1994) at about age 19 as an early Epic MegaGames hit, establishing him as a commercial game designer well before Gears of War.
early_history_summary: Born February 12, 1975. Teen designer who shipped Jazz Jackrabbit with Epic, then became a central design leader at Epic Games on Unreal and Gears of War franchises before later Boss Key Productions.
family_context_summary: American upbringing; detailed parental domain not strongly documented in reviewed sources.
primary_early_advantage_tags: teen commercial game, Epic ecosystem, shareware era, later Gears
evidence_summary: Bleszinski shipped Jazz Jackrabbit at 19—clear material ≤26 milestone—then compounded design leadership inside Epic through Unreal and Gears. Early shareware/Epic ecosystem plus intense design reps dominate the advantage stack.
starting_point: Born 1975; teen game designer who entered Epic MegaGames' shareware scene.
current_position: Game designer and industry personality; after Epic and Boss Key, continues creative projects and public commentary.

trajectory.event: Released Jazz Jackrabbit with Epic MegaGames.
Design leadership roles around Unreal franchise at Epic.
Shipped Gears of War, defining third-person cover shooters on Xbox 360.
Left Epic after Gears trilogy era.
Founded Boss Key Productions (LawBreakers).

name: Jade Raymond
category: Game producer/studio founder (Assassin's Creed, Ubisoft Toronto, Motive)
milestone_by_age_26: Assassin's Creed (2007) at about age 32 is the defining credit; earlier Sony/EA programmer roles are employment without a clear material founder/breakout product by age 26.
evidence_summary: Assassin's Creed (2007) at about age 32 is the defining credit; earlier Sony/EA programmer roles are employment without a clear material founder/breakout product by age 26.

name: Kim Swift
milestone_by_age_26: Led design of Portal (2007) at Valve at about age 24 after DigiPen student project Narbacular Drop was hired into Valve—defining puzzle-game landmark.
early_history_summary: Born 1983. DigiPen student who co-created Narbacular Drop; Valve hired the team and transformed the concept into Portal (2007), where Swift was design lead. Later worked at Airtight, Amazon Game Studios, and other studios.
family_context_summary: Not strongly documented in reviewed sources.
primary_early_advantage_tags: DigiPen, Valve hire, Narbacular Drop team, Portal
evidence_summary: Swift's Portal design leadership at 24 is an elite ≤26 milestone enabled by DigiPen training and Valve absorbing her student team. Peer team + institutional pipeline (DigiPen→Valve) are the dominant early advantages.
starting_point: Born 1983; DigiPen Institute game-design education into Valve via student project acquisition path.
current_position: Senior game design leader across studios after Valve (including Amazon Game Studios and others); Portal remains career-defining.

trajectory.event: Co-created DigiPen student game Narbacular Drop.
Design lead on Valve's Portal, a landmark puzzle game.
Continued design leadership after Valve at other studios.

name: Jenova Chen
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded thatgamecompany in 2006 at about age 25 and released Flow (based on his USC MFA thesis) as a major indie/PSN success defining emotion-focused games.
early_history_summary: Born Shanghai 1981; USC Interactive Media MFA. Thesis game Cloud and Flow led to co-founding thatgamecompany with Kellee Santiago; later Flower and Journey under Sony partnership.
family_context_summary: Born Shanghai; moved into USC MFA path; family financial details not strongly documented in reviewed sources.
primary_early_advantage_tags: USC MFA, Santiago cofounder, Sony PSN indie wave, Flow thesis
evidence_summary: Chen co-founded thatgamecompany and shipped Flow at ~25, translating MFA research into commercial indie success. USC pipeline, Santiago partnership, and Sony digital distribution wave are the core early advantages.
starting_point: Born Shanghai 1981; USC Interactive Media MFA student-turned-founder.
current_position: Co-founder of thatgamecompany; designer behind Flow, Flower, Journey, Sky; continues independent emotional-games studio leadership.

trajectory.event: Created Cloud as USC student work attracting industry attention.
Co-founded thatgamecompany and released Flow.
Released Flower on PlayStation Network.
Released Journey, a landmark multiplayer art game.
Released Sky: Children of the Light, expanding the studio's live service.

name: Kellee Santiago
milestone_by_age_26: Produced Cloud (2005) as USC student work and co-founded thatgamecompany in 2006 near age 26–27; Cloud at age ~26 is the dated creative milestone, with company founding straddling the boundary.
early_history_summary: Born 1979; USC Interactive Media. Partnered with Jenova Chen on Cloud and co-founded thatgamecompany, producing Flow/Flower/Journey era. Later Google, niantic-adjacent work, and indie investing/advising.
family_context_summary: Not strongly documented in reviewed sources.
primary_early_advantage_tags: USC, Chen partnership, indie PSN wave, producer craft
evidence_summary: Santiago's Cloud (2005, ~age 26) and thatgamecompany founding with Chen are the early milestones. Advantage stack is USC pipeline plus exceptional cofounder pairing. Journey-era peak comes after 26.
starting_point: Born 1979; USC Interactive Media MFA environment with Jenova Chen.
current_position: Game industry executive/investor after thatgamecompany; roles spanning Google and indie ecosystem advising.

trajectory.event: Produced Cloud at USC, a widely noted student art game.
Co-founded thatgamecompany with Jenova Chen.
Journey released to critical acclaim under thatgamecompany.
Left thatgamecompany for broader industry roles.

name: Reggie Fils-Aimé
milestone_by_age_26: Became Nintendo of America president/COO in 2006 at about age 45 after Panda Express/P&G/VH1 marketing career; E3 2004 'My name is Reggie' moment at age ~43. No material founder/product milestone by age 26.
evidence_summary: Became Nintendo of America president/COO in 2006 at about age 45 after Panda Express/P&G/VH1 marketing career; E3 2004 'My name is Reggie' moment at age ~43. No material founder/product milestone by age 26.

name: Trip Hawkins
milestone_by_age_26: Founded Electronic Arts in 1982 at about age 28–29 after Apple; 3DO later. No material founder milestone by age 26 (Apple employment does not qualify as personal founder breakout).
evidence_summary: Founded Electronic Arts in 1982 at about age 28–29 after Apple; 3DO later. No material founder milestone by age 26 (Apple employment does not qualify as personal founder breakout).

name: Ralph Baer
milestone_by_age_26: Brown Box / Odyssey work was in his 40s–50s (1960s–1972). WWII immigrant engineer career milestones are not a by-26 founder/product breakout of the home video game system.
evidence_summary: Brown Box / Odyssey work was in his 40s–50s (1960s–1972). WWII immigrant engineer career milestones are not a by-26 founder/product breakout of the home video game system.

name: Steve Russell
milestone_by_age_26: Created Spacewar! on the PDP-1 at MIT around 1961–1962 at about age 24–25, one of the first influential digital video games.
early_history_summary: Born 1937. MIT-associated programmer in the early minicomputer culture who wrote Spacewar! with collaborators on DEC PDP-1, establishing interactive computer gaming's foundational demo.
family_context_summary: Not strongly documented in reviewed sources relative to the MIT/DEC computing milieu.
primary_early_advantage_tags: MIT, PDP-1 access, early hacker culture, Spacewar collaborators
evidence_summary: Russell's Spacewar! at ~25 required scarce PDP-1 access at MIT—rare tools plus elite peer network. Foundational to video game history; commercial industry came later via others. Advantage is institutional/frontier computing access more than family capital.
starting_point: Born 1937; entered MIT/DEC early interactive computing culture with rare hardware access.
current_position: Computer programmer and pioneering game creator; Spacewar! remains his historical legacy; living elder of computing history as of mid-2020s sources.

trajectory.event: Created Spacewar! on the PDP-1 at MIT, founding interactive computer game culture.
Continued computing career as interactive systems spread beyond labs.
Widely celebrated in game-history retrospectives as Spacewar! creator.
